messages.author: 14cad522d99ed9fa
messages.subject: Inconsistent Number of Samples Returned
parts:
I've been running stan via command line with the defaults (2000 iterations, 1000 warmup, thinning = 1), so in theory I should be returning 1000 samples. Most of the time it works fine, but occasionally it returns some other number (I've seen it range anywhere from 961 to 1010 samples). Any idea why this is happening?
 
This also negatively affects the read_stan_csv() function, which returns an error if the number of iterations in the the comments does not match the number of contained samples. I simply changed the number in the comments, but then I get another error:
Error in quantile.default(chain, probs = probs) :
  missing values and NaN's not allowed if 'na.rm' is FALSE
No idea why there would be missing data, but I assume it has to do with Stan returning an odd number of samples.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Inconsistent Number of Samples Returned
parts:
No, we haven't seen that or seen errors like that
reported.

For us to debug, we need to be able to replicate
what you're doing or at least get more of a hint
as to how you're invoking Stan.

Ideally, send us a small example model with data
and a command-line invocation that recreates the
problem. We also need to know what platform you're
running on, which version of Stan you're running,
and which C++ compiler you're using.

If the CSV file is corrupt, read_stan_csv() isn't going
to work.

- Bob
